rationale:
The example `requirements.sdk.graph.search.grouped_constants` describes a concrete case. The query `hit` runs over two constants, `A` with "éhit" and `B` with "hit hit". The expected result is one complete page with two entries: a tag, a node, a file, a selector and an excerpt covering the whole declaration. The test `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs` is marked `{test}` for the example. It covers the scenario like this:

- **Source:** it writes `const A: &str = "éhit"; const B: &str = "hit hit";` to `code.rs`. This is the example's source, and it includes the multi-byte "é".
- **Hits:** it calls `search_text` with `hit` and asserts three hits. One is in `code.rs#const[A]` at 19..22. Two are in `code.rs#const[B]` at 42..45 and 46..49. The two hits in `B` are what the example groups into one entry.
- **Page:** it dispatches the agent tool `search_text` with `{"pattern":"hit"}`, parses the page, and asserts `complete == true`.
- **Entries:** it asserts the `matches` array exactly. It has two entries, not three. The tags are "1" and "2". The nodes are the interned nodes from the hits. The file is `code.rs`. The selectors are `const[A]` and `const[B]`. The excerpts are the full declarations `const A: &str = "éhit";` and `const B: &str = "hit hit";`.

The exact excerpts check the cited requirements:
- `group_hits`: one entry per enclosing item, even with two hits.
- `windows`: the default 128-byte window is clipped to the enclosing item, so A's excerpt does not leak into B. The two windows in B merge into one contiguous excerpt that keeps the text between the hits.

The test also checks that the node reference reads the item and that `finish_search` with tag "2" records a dependency on `const[B]`. This supports the tag and node semantics in `group_hits`.

The example's `search_id` and numeric `node` values are placeholders. The test reasonably uses the real node values and does not assert a random UUID. The example says the page is shown "after the first-search instructions have been delivered". The test asserts only `complete` and `matches`, so an `instructions` field cannot affect it. `Pages::search` adds `instructions` only on the first search, so the asserted fields are unaffected. No acknowledgments are needed, and I found no gap.

text: For the same `hit` query, the agent receives one excerpt per declaration. After the first-search instructions have been delivered, the complete page looks like this.

Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.

The agent's `search_text` tool accepts a nonnegative `window_bytes`, defaulting to 128. For a hit with byte span `[start, end)`, retain the hit and up to `window_bytes` of source immediately before `start` and after `end`. Clip the window to the enclosing item's span. Move a context boundary that splits a UTF-8 character inward to the nearest character boundary. With `window_bytes: 0`, only the hit spans and the available header and trailer contribute source to the excerpt.

Compute windows for all hits in the item from the same snapshot. Where windows touch or overlap, emit the contiguous source once. This preserves each hit and the text between nearby hits, including whitespace and newlines.
